newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Foreign portfolio investment in S.Korea up in June.
newsitem.headline: Foreign portfolio investment in S.Korea up in June.

text.p: Foreign portfolio investment in South Korea marked a net inflow of $1.35 billion in June from $1.29 billion in May, preliminary figures from the central Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Monday.
The central bank attributed the rise to a steady inflow of foreign funds for equity investment and from the sales of beneficary bonds for foreigners.
A BOK statement said a net of $880 million flowed in during June for stock investment, the fourth largest total since the local stock market opened to foreigners in 1992.
This compared with $1.15 billion in May.
The inflow for equity investment was particularly large in May as the foreign stock ownership ceiling was expanded to 23 percent on May 2 from previous 20 percent.

The statement said domestic investment trust firms increased their issuance of beneficiary certificates in line with the market recovery, resulting in a net inflow of $420 million in June against $40 million in May.
Direct investment in the local bond market by foreigners rose to $54.1 million in June, sharply up $0.4 million a month ago, the statement said.
The government allowed foreign direct investment in non-guaranteed listed bonds issued by small- and medium-firms and non-guaranteed listed convertible bonds issued by large companies from June 2.
